## Natural history notes

A tiny songbird characterized by its gray upperparts, whitish underparts, short tail, sharp pointed bill, and distinctive brown cap. In Florida, it is found mainly in mature pine forests, pine flatwoods, sandhills, and open pine woodlands, especially where standing dead trees or old woodpecker cavities provide nesting sites. It feeds mostly on insects, spiders, and other small arthropods, often climbing along pine trunks, branches, and cones while probing bark crevices, and may also eat pine seeds.
